cases.question: Summarise section 190 of the Nigeria Tax Act.

claims.text: Section 190(1) sets rules that apply when trades or businesses are restructured.

On a merger of two or more trades or businesses, a new trade or business is not deemed to have commenced because of the merger. The Act's provisions on cessation of trade or business do not apply to the trade or business that ceased as a result of the merger.
On a merger, the Part VIII of Chapter Two provisions on chargeable gains do not apply to the assets transferred to the new or surviving trade or business.

On a merger, assets of the merging trades or businesses are deemed transferred at the residue of the qualifying capital expenditure on the day following the merger. The First Schedule applies on the remaining useful life of the asset transferred.

On a merger, unutilised capital allowance on the assets transferred is available for the new or surviving trade or business. Taxes deducted at source for the merged trades or businesses are available to the merged trade or business.
On a merger, unabsorbed losses of the merging entities are available to the surviving trade or business, provided that the merged trade or business incurred those losses.

On a sale or transfer of a trade or business that results in its cessation, the Part V of Chapter Two provisions on cessation apply to the trade or business sold or transferred. The assets are recognised at the value at which they are sold or transferred for the First Schedule. The Part VIII of Chapter Two chargeable gains provisions apply to any asset sold or transferred.

On a sale or transfer that results in cessation, unutilised capital allowance on the assets, unabsorbed losses of the old business, and taxes deducted at source from the old business are not available for use by the new or surviving trade or business.

On a sale or transfer of a business asset that does not result in cessation, where the parties agreed an amount not exceeding the sum of the residue of the qualifying capital expenditure and unutilised capital allowance of the asset, capital allowance under the First Schedule applies to the residue of the asset only.

In that case, the unutilised capital allowance on the asset is available for use by the buying trade or business. The seller cannot claim any part of it. The Part VIII of Chapter Two chargeable gains provisions do not apply to the asset.

For companies in upstream petroleum operations, where restructuring forms a new company and ends the old business, the acquiring company's accounting period starts on the date of the sale or transfer. It can instead start on a date within that calendar month that the company elects with the Service's approval. It ends on 31 December of the same year, and any gap between the old and surviving business is treated as part of the new or surviving company. This applies notwithstanding subsection (1).
That period is the "Accounting Period" under Chapter Three of the Act.
The relevant tax authority is to be notified of any restructuring of a trade, business, profession or vocation prior to commencing the arrangement.
References in section 190 to a trade or business include references to any part of the trade or business.
VAT charged under Chapter Six of the Act does not apply to business restructuring carried out in accordance with the Act.

A transfer of a business, or a part capable of separate operation, as a going concern is not treated as a supply of goods or services for VAT. This applies where the purchaser uses the assets in the same kind of business, and the purchaser is registered under Part II of the Nigeria Tax Administration Act, 2025 or registerable as a result of the transfer.
Section 157 applies section 190 to the sale or transfer of a trade, business, profession or vocation carried on in Nigeria.

cases.question: When does a sale count as made for VAT: when I send the invoice, when I deliver, or when I get paid?

claims.text: A taxable supply is deemed to take place at the time an invoice or receipt is issued by the supplier, or where goods are delivered or made available for use, or payment is due to or received by the supplier in respect of that supply, whichever occurs first.

Where the supplier and recipient are connected persons and invoices are not issued, a supply of goods not to be removed is deemed to take place at the time when they are available to the recipient.
Where the supplier and recipient are connected persons and invoices are not issued, furnishing of a service is deemed to take place upon commencement of the furnishing of the service.
Where the supplier and recipient are connected persons and invoices are not issued, an incorporeal is deemed supplied when it becomes available for the use of the recipient.

Notwithstanding the general rule, goods supplied under a rental agreement, or services furnished under an agreement or law providing for periodic payments, are deemed to be successively supplied for successive parts of the periods. Each successive supply is deemed to occur when payment becomes due or is received, whichever is earlier.

Notwithstanding the general rule, taxable supplies made progressively or periodically, or in relation to construction, assembly, manufacturing, alteration, improvement or repair under an agreement providing for payment in instalments or periodically, are deemed to be successively made. Each successive supply is deemed to take place whenever any payment becomes due or is received or an invoice relating to only that payment is issued, whichever occurs first.

Notwithstanding the general rule, where a taxable supply is made under an instalment credit agreement, the supply is deemed to take place at the time the taxable supply is delivered or the time any payment of consideration is received by the supplier in respect of the supply, whichever occurs first.

claims.text: Tax is levied for each year of assessment on the total profits of every company. A company that is not a small company pays at the rate of 30 per cent from the commencement of the Act.
